title: Trapezoidal head-exchange iteration and coupling stiffness
purpose: Freeze a discrete temporal exchange closure and compare explicit, one-corrector and fixed-point behavior without management clipping, so iteration behavior can be derived and tested independently of shortage policy.

frozen_temporal_contract.managed_delivery: U is frozen within the numerical sub-experiment
frozen_temporal_contract.groundwater_head: h_gw is fixed within one coupling window

derived_hypothesis.implication: simple Picard exchange iteration converges for lambda < 1, is neutral/oscillatory at lambda = 1, and diverges for lambda > 1

experiments.T1: closed-form fixed point satisfies both trapezoidal exchange equation and water-balance end-level equation
experiments.T2: lambda < 1 gives alternating geometric Picard convergence with error ratio -lambda
experiments.T3: lambda = 1 gives equal-magnitude alternating error from a non-exact initial guess
experiments.T4: lambda > 1 gives growing error magnitude with ratio lambda
experiments.T5: one corrector improves the explicit start-level estimate when lambda < 1 but is not exact in general
experiments.T6: parameter sets with equal lambda have the same normalized Picard error propagation
experiments.T7: managed delivery U shifts the fixed point but does not change the Picard error factor
experiments.T8: reducing dt enough to move lambda from above one to below one restores Picard convergence

interpretation_rules: lambda is a property of this frozen linear trapezoidal surrogate, not a universal MODFLOW-Ribasim stability theorem
no convergence tolerance is introduced; tests use the exact analytic error relation
management clipping and shortage feedback are deliberately excluded from DUMMY-04
a later work unit may reintroduce DUMMY-02 management priority after the numerical mechanism is qualified
forbidden: no production solver or coupling change
no claim that trapezoidal exchange is the unique correct temporal discretization
